title: Durable reversal of diabetic kidney disease

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a safe treatment that durably repairs established kidney damage caused by diabetes, restoring useful kidney function as well as improving tissue structure. It would work without requiring a pancreas transplant and would have a kidney-directed benefit that can be distinguished from the effects of improved glucose control. The intended advance is repair of existing damage, extending beyond protection against further deterioration.

Diabetic kidney disease affects several connected parts of the kidney. The documented abnormalities include thickened glomerular and tubular basement membranes, expansion of the mesangial tissue that supports the filtering structures, interstitial changes, vascular abnormalities and glomerular scarring. Repair therefore cannot be assessed through a single lesion alone: remodeling damaged supporting tissue, restoring filtration and replacing permanently lost cells or filtering units are different capabilities. The supplied evidence demonstrates some human tissue remodeling, but does not establish replacement of lost podocytes or nephrons.

significance.text: If a treatment could produce durable structural repair together with restored function across a substantial patient population, it would add a major therapeutic capability in a common cause of chronic kidney disease. Its direct value would be recovering and preserving kidney function and preventing kidney failure. The clinical importance of this goal is supported by the residual progression described in FLOW, while the pancreas-transplant study provides evidence that characteristic diabetic lesions can remodel in humans. Neither result establishes that a broadly usable repair treatment has been achieved.

Structural improvement must not be treated as equivalent to functional recovery. In the pancreas-transplant study, lesion regression did not establish restored filtration, recovery from kidney failure or regeneration of lost filtering units. Similarly, FLOW's cardiovascular findings concern semaglutide; they cannot be transferred to a hypothetical repair treatment. Any claim that kidney repair also reduces cardiovascular mortality would require its own clinical evidence.

Conditional downstream possibilities include fewer people needing dialysis or transplantation and reduced dependence on kidney-replacement capacity. These are reasoned implications of successfully preventing kidney failure, not demonstrated outcomes of the proposed innovation. Their magnitude would depend on the disease stages that remain repairable, how broadly treatment works, its safety and durability, and practical access.

missing_breakthrough.text: The capability sought is coordinated, durable repair of damaged filtering and supporting tissue with a corresponding functional benefit. The supplied studies establish separate pieces of the rationale—clinical protection and human structural remodeling—but do not demonstrate this broadly usable capability. Because the supplied freshness record is empty, these dated studies also cannot establish whether such a capability remains unavailable as of November 1, 2026.

An engineering inference from the documented pathology is that a successful treatment must remodel abnormal tissue while preserving the organization needed for filtration. It must also show that improved tissue measurements translate into sustained kidney performance rather than merely a change in appearance. The transplant findings leave an additional practical challenge: obtaining repair without pancreas transplantation, prolonged transplant-associated normoglycemia or dependence on an immunosuppressive regimen whose effects complicate functional interpretation.

A separate unresolved barrier is the boundary between repairable tissue and permanent loss. The supplied sources do not determine whether lost podocytes or nephrons can be replaced, whether replacement is necessary at particular disease stages, or how much function can return in advanced disease. These are proposed regenerative targets and scientific questions, rather than established prerequisites for every useful degree of diabetic kidney repair.

current_state.text: FLOW, published online on May 24, 2024, demonstrated clinical kidney protection with semaglutide in selected people with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease. The risk of its primary composite outcome, encompassing serious kidney events and kidney or cardiovascular death, was 24% lower with semaglutide than with placebo. It also showed slower decline in estimated kidney function. Mean estimated glomerular filtration rate nevertheless continued to decline in both groups, and the trial did not establish structural repair or a cure.

FLOW does not establish benefit beyond every contemporary combination of kidney-protective treatments. Its discussion identifies modest baseline use of SGLT2 inhibitors and nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid-receptor antagonists as a limitation on evaluating combination therapy. This matters when defining the comparator for a future repair treatment: a benefit against FLOW's placebo group cannot automatically be interpreted as an additional benefit over all current treatment combinations.

Fioretto and colleagues, published on July 9, 1998, documented regression of characteristic diabetic kidney lesions after ten years of normoglycemia in eight selected people with type 1 diabetes and functioning pancreas transplants. These participants did not have uremia at baseline. Biopsy measurements showed reductions in basement-membrane thickness and mesangial expansion, providing human evidence of substantial remodeling of glomerular and tubular structures.

The transplant result has important selection and functional limits. Two members of the original cohort subsequently received kidney transplants and were excluded from the eight-person follow-up. Mean creatinine clearance fell from baseline and then stabilized, and cyclosporine's effects on filtration complicated interpretation. The authors attributed the structural improvement most likely to prolonged normoglycemia. The study therefore supports the possibility of lesion regression under specific conditions, without demonstrating a broadly applicable, glucose-independent repair treatment, restored filtration or recovery from kidney failure.

The supplied review assessed complete, untruncated main-article text for both publications. Figure images were not inspected, and FLOW's supplements were not inspected; the structural conclusions described here rely on the reviewed results text and tabulated morphometry rather than independent inspection of micrographs. No freshness assessment beyond these dated findings was supplied. These limitations constrain interpretation and present-day completeness; they do not negate the reported results.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: controlled trials in people with established diabetic kidney disease should show sustained improvement in measured kidney function and clinically meaningful kidney outcomes alongside structural evidence of repair. The studies should prespecify the magnitude and duration of benefit required, how repair will be assessed and what constitutes an acceptable safety profile. Structural improvement alone or slower functional decline alone would demonstrate only part of the intended capability. These are proposed criteria, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Sustained kidney function and clinical improvements with structural repair

completion_criteria.text: Proposed attribution requirements: demonstrate additional benefit over an appropriately contemporary kidney-protective treatment regimen, and use a design that distinguishes kidney-directed repair from differences in glucose control. Account for other treatment effects that could alter filtration measurements or complicate interpretation. A practical demonstration should establish whether repair requires ongoing treatment and whether benefit persists for a prespecified follow-up period.
completion_criteria.label: Additional kidney-directed repair beyond contemporary treatment and glucose control

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and scope requirements: confirm the structural and functional findings across independent centers and adequately characterized patient groups. Evaluate advanced disease separately, reporting baseline function, the extent of tissue damage, treatment burden and the limits of recovery. Demonstrated benefit in selected populations would establish that breadth of applicability; finite trials would not establish reversal at every disease stage or in every patient. Claims of podocyte replacement, new-nephron formation, reversal of kidney failure or cardiovascular survival benefit would each require evidence specific to that outcome.
completion_criteria.label: Structural and functional repair reproduced across independent centers

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: NEP-02, “Rebuild function in scarred kidneys by reversing established fibrosis,” has a clear potential overlap with the scarring component of diabetic kidney disease. NEP-09 remains a distinct disease-specific target because its scope also includes characteristic glomerular, tubular and mesangial abnormalities. The supplied roster establishes NEP-02's title and broad aim, but its detailed entry was not supplied, so the precise mechanistic overlap remains unverified.

Roster-based comparison: NEP-01, “Regrow functional nephrons inside an adult human kidney,” could become relevant where diabetic disease has destroyed filtering units. NEP-09 does not inherently require new-nephron formation if useful function can be recovered by repairing surviving structures. NEP-03, “Manufacture transplantable human kidneys from cells,” and NEP-06, “An effectively unlimited supply of durable animal-donor kidneys,” instead seek replacement organs. NEP-07, “Reliably induce donor-specific tolerance in kidney recipients,” addresses acceptance of a donor organ; the pancreas-transplant evidence for NEP-09 does not make transplant tolerance the same innovation.

Roster-based comparison: NEP-04, “A durable, implantable artificial kidney,” and NEP-05, “Kidney replacement that is portable and affordable at global scale,” pursue replacement of kidney function through devices or services. NEP-09 seeks recovery of the patient's own damaged kidneys. Successful repair could reduce demand for those replacement approaches, while patients beyond the demonstrated repair boundary could still need them.

Roster-based comparison: NEP-08, “A root-cause, durable treatment for ADPKD,” shares the ambition of durable treatment for a specific kidney disease, but targets a different disease process. NEP-10, “Broad prevention of severe acute kidney injury,” focuses on preventing acute injury, whereas NEP-09 concerns reversal of established diabetes-associated damage. These entries may share outcome measures or future repair tools, but their disease targets and intended interventions remain distinct.

unresolved_issues: Whether subsequent evidence establishes a broadly usable repair capability as of November 1, 2026 remains unassessed.
The extent to which advanced diabetic kidney disease or established kidney failure can be reversed is unresolved.
Whether lost podocytes or nephrons can be replaced, and when such replacement would be necessary for meaningful recovery, is unresolved by the supplied sources.
The treatment mechanism, acceptable safety profile, required effect size, durability period and need for ongoing treatment remain unspecified.
Broad reproducibility and additional benefit over contemporary combinations of kidney-protective therapies remain to be demonstrated for any proposed repair treatment.
The precise relationship with NEP-02 and other roster concepts cannot be established from titles alone.
Figure images and FLOW supplements were not inspected in the supplied review; no conclusions requiring those materials have been added.

brief.title: Lasting repair of kidney damage from diabetes
possible: People whose kidneys have been damaged by diabetes could regain useful kidney function through a safe treatment that repairs existing damage. The repair would last, would not require a pancreas transplant, and would have benefits beyond those of better blood sugar control.
why: Recovering and preserving kidney function could help people with diabetes avoid kidney failure. Fewer people could need dialysis, which filters the blood when kidneys cannot, or a kidney transplant.

sources.who: Vlado Perkovic and the FLOW Trial Committees and Investigators
sources.showed: In selected people with diabetes and chronic kidney disease, semaglutide lowered the combined risk of serious kidney events or kidney or cardiovascular death by 24%. Kidney function declined more slowly.
sources.quote:
Semaglutide reduced the risk of clinically important kidney outcomes and death 
from cardiovascular causes in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney 
disease.
sources.cited_for: The trial supports kidney protection while showing that loss of kidney function can continue despite treatment.
sources.not_established: The trial did not demonstrate repair of damaged kidney tissue or restored kidney function.

sources.who: Paola Fioretto, Michael Steffes, David Sutherland, Frederick Goetz and Michael Mauer
sources.showed: A small, selected group with functioning pancreas transplants had less thickening and excess supporting tissue in their kidneys after prolonged normal blood sugar. Kidney filtration did not recover.
sources.quote:
Pancreas transplantation can reverse
the lesions of diabetic nephropathy, but reversal re-
quires more than five years of normoglycemia.
sources.cited_for: Characteristic kidney tissue damage from diabetes can regress in humans.
sources.not_established: The study did not demonstrate restored filtration or repair achievable without transplantation and prolonged normal blood sugar.

shown: Fioretto and colleagues found substantial tissue improvement in eight selected pancreas transplant recipients. This shows that some kidney damage from diabetes can remodel, but their average filtration fell before stabilizing.
The FLOW investigators showed that semaglutide slowed kidney function loss and reduced serious outcomes. Average kidney function still declined, and the trial did not demonstrate tissue repair.
missing: A safe treatment must produce lasting tissue repair together with improved kidney function and meaningful clinical benefits.
Repair must work without a pancreas transplant and add benefits beyond current kidney protection and better blood sugar control.
Independent centers must reproduce structural and functional recovery across clearly described patient groups.

milestones.label: Lasting functional recovery alongside tissue repair
milestones.explanation: Controlled trials would have to show sustained kidney function gains, better clinical outcomes and tissue repair, with defined benefit and safety thresholds. This would establish repair that improves how kidneys work.

milestones.label: Repair beyond current care and blood sugar control
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to distinguish kidney repair from blood sugar effects, show added benefit over current care and establish durability and ongoing treatment needs. This would identify a practical, kidney-directed benefit.

milestones.label: Recovery reproduced across independent centers
milestones.explanation: Independent centers would have to reproduce tissue and functional recovery in defined patient groups, assessing advanced disease separately. This would establish who benefits and where recovery reaches its limits.

uncertain: How much function can return in advanced disease or established kidney failure remains unresolved.
It is unclear whether lost filtering cells or whole filtering units can be replaced, or when replacement is needed for useful recovery.
The required size and duration of benefit, acceptable safety profile and need for ongoing treatment remain undefined.

page.title: Reversal of diabetic kidney disease
page.definition: A treatment repairs established kidney lesions caused by diabetes and recovers lost filtration, the removal of water and solutes from blood. Structural and functional gains persist during follow-up without pancreas transplantation, with kidney benefit distinguishable from improved glucose control.

goal.need: In 2021, diabetes caused 60,113 new cases of kidney failure requiring dialysis or transplantation in the United States. In adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, estimated filtration fell by an average of 2.19 mL/min/1.73 m² per year with semaglutide and 3.36 with placebo. Recovering filtration already lost could give patients more time before they need dialysis or a transplant, if the gain is large enough and lasts. In-center hemodialysis typically takes four hours three times a week.

figures.note: Estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) slopes are in mL/min/1.73 m²/year. The primary composite included kidney failure, ≥50% eGFR reduction, or kidney-related or cardiovascular death.

completion.title: A controlled human trial confirms sustained structural and functional reversal of diabetic kidney disease.
completion.criterion: A controlled human trial demonstrates regression of established diabetic kidney lesions on paired biopsies and recovery above baseline of impaired measured glomerular filtration rate, both maintained through prospectively specified durability follow-up. Treatment does not require pancreas transplantation; background kidney care and glucose control permit attribution to a kidney-directed effect. The trial meets its prespecified efficacy and safety criteria. No externally agreed minimum effect size or durability interval was found; those quantities require definition in the registered protocol.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no published joint structural, functional and durability threshold was found.
completion.basis: No external standard was identified for sustained recovery of both kidney structure and filtration. After pancreas transplantation, diabetic lesions regressed at ten years while mean creatinine clearance remained below baseline. In type 2 diabetes, TSUBAKI demonstrated a rise in filtration measured by inulin clearance at 16 weeks. REMODEL examined paired biopsies but did not establish recovery of directly measured filtration. FLOW demonstrated slower loss of estimated filtration.

milestones.title: A kidney-directed treatment shows preclinical biological activity and a feasible administration route.
milestones.criterion: For cellular or gene therapies, establish biological plausibility, active doses, and feasibility and reasonable safety of administration in relevant preclinical systems. FDA specifies no numerical diabetic-reversal cutoff. In a published ZSF1 diabetic-rat experiment, selected renal cells reduced serum creatinine at 16 weeks after treatment: 44.2 versus 53.0 µmol/L in untreated rats, n=5 per group, P=0.014. This demonstrates animal bioactivity, not satisfaction of every FDA preclinical requirement.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Preclinical Assessment of Investigational Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, sections III.A–B; nonbinding recommendations for cellular and gene products. The cited animal result concerns a type 2 diabetes model.
milestones.threshold_quote: Establishment of feasibility and reasonable safety of the investigational product’s proposed clinical route of administration (ROA).

milestones.title: The week-1 safety review permits escalation from 150 million to 300 million rexlemestrocel-L cells.
milestones.criterion: After every participant in the first cohort completes the week-1 visit, the independent monitoring committee reviews safety and issues a certificate of non-objection before escalation. The protocol calls for holding enrollment or recommending termination for any grade 4 or higher pulmonary or upper respiratory toxicity at any time after infusion, or any grade 3 or higher immune system toxicity within 7 days, under the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events.
milestones.set_by: Mesoblast and the independent Data Monitoring Committee, registered rexlemestrocel-L protocol NCT01843387, reported by Packham et al.; written for type 2 diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: issued a certificate of non-objection to advance

milestones.title: Paired human kidney biopsies show regression of established diabetic lesions.
milestones.criterion: Compare quantitative measurements from kidney biopsies taken from the same participants before and after intervention. A diabetic lesion documented at baseline must regress, for example through thinning of an abnormally thick glomerular basement membrane or a reduction in the fraction of the glomerulus occupied by expanded mesangium.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback. No common minimum reduction was identified. Fioretto and colleagues provide a paired-biopsy benchmark in type 1 diabetes.

milestones.title: Rilparencel delays the first qualifying kidney event or cardiovascular death versus sham.
milestones.criterion: In the randomized, blinded phase 3 comparison in type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, the prespecified time-to-first-event analysis must favour rilparencel over sham. Count from first injection to the earliest of a ≥40% fall in estimated GFR sustained for 30 days, estimated GFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m² sustained for 30 days, chronic dialysis, kidney transplantation, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes. Estimate GFR with the 2021 CKD-EPI serum creatinine equation.
milestones.set_by: ProKidney, REGEN-006/PROACT 1 protocol NCT05099770, clinical endpoint.
milestones.threshold_quote: At least 40% reduction in eGFR, sustained for 30 days, OR

milestones.title: A controlled human study shows both diabetic lesion regression and recovery of impaired filtration.
milestones.criterion: A controlled human study must show regression of established diabetic lesions on paired kidney biopsies and a rise above baseline in initially impaired, directly measured glomerular filtration rate in the same participants. The comparison must distinguish the kidney effect from differences in glucose control and background kidney care. This milestone concerns the initial response before confirmation of its durability.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback after searches of FDA guidance and renal cell-therapy protocols found no joint biopsy-and-filtration recovery threshold.

milestones.title: Preclinical testing identifies a dose of a cell or gene therapy with activity against diabetic kidney injury.
milestones.criterion: Establish biological plausibility and identify a biologically active dose for the proposed kidney indication in a relevant preclinical system.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Preclinical Assessment of Investigational Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, sections III.A–B, nonbinding preclinical programme objectives.
milestones.threshold_quote: Identification of biologically active dose levels.

milestones.title: Preclinical testing shows that the proposed clinical route is feasible and reasonably safe.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate the feasibility and reasonable safety of administering the investigational kidney cell or gene therapy by its proposed clinical route.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Preclinical Assessment of Investigational Cellular and Gene Therapy Products, section III.A, nonbinding preclinical programme objectives.
milestones.threshold_quote: Establishment of feasibility and reasonable safety of the investigational product’s proposed clinical route of administration (ROA).

milestones.title: Bardoxolone improves 16-week change in measured filtration versus placebo in stage 3 kidney disease.
milestones.criterion: In the TSUBAKI stage 3 cohort with type 2 diabetes, baseline estimated GFR of 30 to <60 mL/min/1.73 m² and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio <300 mg/g, compare change from baseline to week 16 in GFR measured by inulin clearance. The prespecified group-sequential analysis in the per-protocol population must favour bardoxolone methyl over placebo, with overall one-sided alpha 0.025.
milestones.set_by: TSUBAKI registered phase 2 protocol NCT02316821, stage 3 primary efficacy analysis reported by Nangaku and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: change from baseline in GFR measured by inulin clearance at week 16

not_found: No published minimum effect size or follow-up duration was found for combined structural and functional reversal of diabetic kidney disease.
No statement disputing reversal as a treatment goal was found in the diabetes research programmes or nephrology guidance examined.

results.finding: In type 1-like diabetic mice (n=6 per group), intravenous hUC-MSCs reduced urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio at a dose of 5 × 10⁵ cells.
results.detail: Kidney abnormalities improved without changes in blood glucose, and the authors reported no adverse effects. The study provides biological plausibility and an active intravenous dose, but its two-week follow-up and limited safety reporting do not establish the full preclinical safety criterion.
results.quote: However, for both experiments, uACR was lower in recipients of hUC-MSC injections than in those injected with NS.

results.finding: In 8 adults with type 1 diabetes, mean glomerular basement membrane thickness fell by 190 nm on paired biopsies after pancreas transplantation.
results.detail: Glomerular basement membrane thickness first showed a significant decrease at the 10-year biopsy.

results.quote: Single intravenous injections of hUC-MSCs ameliorated glomerular abnormalities and interstitial fibrosis in a male mouse model of STZ-induced diabetes without affecting hyperglycemia, whether administered at relatively short or longer duration of diabetes.

goal.need = "In 2021, diabetes caused 60,113 new cases of kidney failure requiring dialysis or transplantation in the United States. In adults with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, estimated filtration fell by an average of 2.19 mL/min/1.73 m\u00b2 per year with semaglutide and 3.36 with placebo. Recovering filtration already lost could give patients more time before they need dialysis or a transplant, if the gain is large enough and lasts. In-center hemodialysis typically takes four hours three times a week.". Reason: The trial enrollment count gives no measure of the population burden, and the original paragraph omits what recovered filtration could mean for a patient.

add statement by National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, 1997: "limit, or reverse renal lesions due to this disorder.". Reason: The 1997 funding announcement directly identifies reversal of diabetic kidney lesions as an intervention goal.

add statement by JDRF, 2021: "developing treatments that can delay, prevent, or reverse diabetic kidney disease.". Reason: JDRF explicitly included reversal in its treatment goals for kidney disease in people with type 1 diabetes.

add not found: "No statement disputing reversal as a treatment goal was found in the diabetes research programmes or nephrology guidance examined.". Reason: The institutional statements establish support for reversal and leave the question of institutional opposition unanswered.

edit completion: basis = "No external standard was identified for sustained recovery of both kidney structure and filtration. After pancreas transplantation, diabetic lesions regressed at ten years while mean creatinine clearance remained below baseline. In type 2 diabetes, TSUBAKI demonstrated a rise in filtration measured by inulin clearance at 16 weeks. REMODEL examined paired biopsies but did not establish recovery of directly measured filtration. FLOW demonstrated slower loss of estimated filtration."; refs = [1, 4, 13, 17]. Reason: The basis omits a positive trial of directly measured filtration and a randomized paired-biopsy trial, both of which clarify what remains to be demonstrated.

split m1 into "Preclinical testing identifies a dose of a cell or gene therapy with activity against diabetic kidney injury." | "Preclinical testing shows that the proposed clinical route is feasible and reasonably safe.". Reason: FDA lists biological activity and the feasibility and safety of delivery as separate preclinical objectives, and an animal efficacy result can establish one without establishing the other.

edit m2: title = "The week-1 safety review permits escalation from 150 million to 300 million rexlemestrocel-L cells."; criterion = "After every participant in the first cohort completes the week-1 visit, the independent monitoring committee reviews safety and issues a certificate of non-objection before escalation. The protocol calls for holding enrollment or recommending termination for any grade 4 or higher pulmonary or upper respiratory toxicity at any time after infusion, or any grade 3 or higher immune system toxicity within 7 days, under the Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events."; threshold_quote = "issued a certificate of non-objection to advance"; threshold_ref = 6. Reason: The protocol makes escalation contingent on the committee's week-1 review, while its pulmonary stopping rule applies at any time after infusion.

edit m3: criterion = "Compare quantitative measurements from kidney biopsies taken from the same participants before and after intervention. A diabetic lesion documented at baseline must regress, for example through thinning of an abnormally thick glomerular basement membrane or a reduction in the fraction of the glomerulus occupied by expanded mesangium."; set_by = "Atlas fallback. No common minimum reduction was identified. Fioretto and colleagues provide a paired-biopsy benchmark in type 1 diabetes."; refs = [4, 13]. Reason: The original criterion embeds one cohort's measurements and attrition, obscuring the comparison that establishes lesion regression.

add milestone after m3: "Bardoxolone improves 16-week change in measured filtration versus placebo in stage 3 kidney disease.". Reason: The entry has a milestone for biopsy-proven repair but lacks the corresponding controlled human test of filtration measured directly.

edit m4: title = "Rilparencel delays the first qualifying kidney event or cardiovascular death versus sham."; criterion = "In the randomized, blinded phase 3 comparison in type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, the prespecified time-to-first-event analysis must favour rilparencel over sham. Count from first injection to the earliest of a \u226540% fall in estimated GFR sustained for 30 days, estimated GFR <15 mL/min/1.73 m\u00b2 sustained for 30 days, chronic dialysis, kidney transplantation, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes. Estimate GFR with the 2021 CKD-EPI serum creatinine equation."; set_by = "ProKidney, REGEN-006/PROACT 1 protocol NCT05099770, clinical endpoint."; threshold_quote = "At least 40% reduction in eGFR, sustained for 30 days, OR"; threshold_ref = 19; refs = [19, 7]. Reason: The registered clinical endpoint measures time from first injection to the first qualifying event and is distinct from the trial's intermediate filtration-slope endpoint.
remove not found 1. Reason: The sponsor's ClinicalTrials.gov record supplies the clinical endpoint and distinguishes it from the intermediate endpoint.

edit m5: criterion = "A controlled human study must show regression of established diabetic lesions on paired kidney biopsies and a rise above baseline in initially impaired, directly measured glomerular filtration rate in the same participants. The comparison must distinguish the kidney effect from differences in glucose control and background kidney care. This milestone concerns the initial response before confirmation of its durability."; refs = [4, 8, 13, 17]. Reason: The original criterion reports a change in estimated filtration slope from a study that did not test the combined biopsy and measured-filtration endpoint.
remove statement 1. Reason: The committee described reversing glycation to prevent sclerosis, which is a different goal from repairing established diabetic kidney lesions.

remove statement 0. Reason: The budget passage addresses restoration of kidney function across kidney diseases, whereas NIDDK's diabetes-specific funding announcement names the relevant lesions explicitly.
